question.problem:
The random variable $X$ has the following probability distribution.

| $x$ | $-3$ | $-\sqrt{3}$ | $0$ | $\sqrt{3}$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.3$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ | $0.3$ | $0.2$ |

Calculate $P({X}^{2}=3).$

current_example.problem:
The random variable $X$ has the following probability distribution.

| $x$ | $-4$ | $-2$ | $0$ | $2$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.3$ | $0.2$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ | $0.3$ |

Calculate $P(X^2 = 4).$
current_example.worked_solution:
Let's first add an $X^2$ row to our table.

| $x$ | $-4$ | $-2$ | $0$ | $2$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x^2$ | $16$ | $4$ | $0$ | $4$ | $16$ |
| $f(x)$ | $0.3$ | $0.2$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ | $0.3$ |

From the second and third rows of our table, we can immediately conclude that 

$$
P(X^2 = 4) = 0.2+0.1 = 0.3.
$$
